significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that, for the same unknown entity, the model's "'I don't know this' signal still fires" in both generation modes but causally gates attribute extraction only when directly queried, producing refusal in one regime and confident fabrication in the other; this is a form-(ii) causal decomposition, with the secondary "fabrication scales with continuation pressure while the probe stays constant" constituting a form-(iii) dependence if also established. It would establish both a paired behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism separating recognition from use, constraining whether query-based self-knowledge findings such as Kadavath et al.'s Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know and uncertainty methods such as Kuhn et al.'s semantic-entropy work can explain fabrication during unconstrained continuation. The negative branches are also determinate and informative: mode-independent fabrication supports a common gating account, whereas a weaker spontaneous probe supports recognition failure rather than gate bypass. Topic-substitution check: the broad topic of knowledge retrieval alone would not justify this score; the specific present-but-decoupled, mode-dependent decomposition is what raises it above the topic-median probe-and-steer hypothesis.

reach.justification: The claim names two usable handles: "free-generation probes" for auditing and "mid-generation re-gating" of the recognition signal, with the latter acting ex ante at the entity position before fabricated attributes are emitted rather than merely explaining an existing error. After per-model re-extraction, the asserted conclusion predicts a relation—recognition remains approximately constant while gating and fabrication vary with generation mode and continuation pressure—rather than supplying only a procedure for rediscovering an arbitrary direction. The stated scope includes transfer "across entity types and models," and downstream users include safety-evaluation designers, refusal-training practitioners, and model auditors who could screen or intervene before deployment or emission, although frontier-scale and cross-architecture generality remain conditional parts of the hypothesis. Topic-substitution check: removing the provoked-versus-spontaneous relation and generation-time handles leaves only the general knowledge-retrieval topic, which would not retain this reach score.
